griddle-amber.note: The page ground. Painted as a fixed four-stop gradient in oklab: #f2860f 0%, #f7a70f 26%, #f9c614 58%, #fae51a 100%. The token is the mid stop, which is what any flat background use resolves to.

buffalo-orange.note: Sampled from the live site (237 instances), not invented. 5.4:1 on char, 1.8:1 on the amber ground, 2.6:1 on parchment.

char.note: Not pure black. A trace of blue keeps large dark areas from looking dead beside warm food photography. Roughly 11:1 against the amber ground.

warm-bone.note: Reading colour on dark surfaces. Warm off-white rather than pure white, so long copy on near-black does not glare.

parchment.note: The chrome surface, always paired with Cream as a gradient so the navbar and footer are never one flat tone. Black type measures 15:1 at the deepest stop.

signage-yellow.note: Extremely high contrast on ink, which is why it is rationed to badges, micro-labels and the bottom stop of the heat scale. Never a paragraph.

buffalo-red.note: A display colour that cannot carry a label. Bone on it measures 3.8:1 and char 4.6:1. Two jobs only: the top of the heat scale, and a destructive icon accent on hover.

red-deep.note: The destructive fill on engagement. Warm bone measures 5.2:1 here and 6.8:1 on Red Deeper, which is what lets a destructive control be unmistakably red and still read as considered.

hero.purpose: The landing headline and nothing else. The 6rem cap is real: Anton past that becomes a texture rather than a headline. Excluded from balanced wrapping because it sets its own breaks.

page.purpose: Every route title that is not the landing hero: menu, category, cart, checkout, about, contact.

panel.purpose: The heading inside a card. Small on purpose, so it does not outrank the number underneath it, and tracked because Anton at 14px in caps closes up.

body.purpose: All reading copy. Inter, chosen because it holds at 14px on a phone. Orphan control is applied globally.

label.purpose: A data caption or the name of the thing the number beside it measures. Family-agnostic: this role is worn by all three faces depending on what it labels, and only the metrics are shared.

numeric.purpose: Every number the user reads, compares or says out loud. Prices, order codes, pickup codes, countdowns, quantities, heat percentages. Tabular figures so columns align and digits do not reflow.

script.purpose: The store's fixed tagline, '#Your All Time Favorite Chicken Wings', and nothing else on the site. Lettering rather than type: it is part of the lockup, never takes a variable string, never sets a heading, label, control or price, and is never uppercased because a brush script's joins are drawn for lowercase. Two placements (landing hero, one paragraph on About), both at 1.5rem below sm and 1.75rem from sm, the hero alone dropping to 1.25rem under max-height 500px. One content placement per page; the footer's mark is chrome and is exempt. Never Buffalo Orange: 1.8:1 on amber and 2.2:1 at the top of the hero scrim, and this face has the thinnest joins in the system. The tagline has two renderings and the shape of the space picks between them. Where a roughly 2:1 block fits, use the delivered artwork (components/brand/TaglineMark.tsx): three interlocking diagonal lines, floor w-[220px] sm:w-[260px], set by the keyline falling to 0.89px at 220 and dropping out below about 200. That artwork cannot become one line; the trimmed master has zero blank rows across 463 and no rotation separates the bands. Where the space is a single line, use .tagline-inked, which paints the lockup's own treatment (signage yellow, black keyline, black offset shadow, paint-order stroke fill) onto the face the artwork is set in. Hero uses the class; footer uses the artwork; About stays ink on amber.

shadows.name: chrome-float
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. The sticky bar overlaps the hero video and needs to sit above it rather than butt against it with a hard seam. Warm and offset, because a neutral grey shadow on a warm page reads as dirt.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every hover and focus transition on a control. Colour and border only, never size, so nothing reflows under the cursor.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The shared press. Answers immediately and releases lazily, which is what makes a control feel connected to the finger. Pinned to scale(1) under reduced motion, because a zero duration on a transform still moves it, just instantly.

motion.name: heat-reveal
motion.value: transform 640ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), staggered 70ms per stop, horizontal at every width
motion.purpose: The site only authored animation: the five stops of the heat ramp drawing themselves in sequence as the band arrives, rightward as rows on a phone and upward as columns from sm. Transform only, so nothing reflows. The drawn state is the default, so no-JS and reduced motion both keep it.

motion.name: tile-photo
motion.purpose: The product photograph on hover inside its clipped frame.

narrative.overview:
The whole system is the branded greaseproof sheet the wings actually arrive on. A warm printed ground that runs hot at the top and cools to signage yellow at the bottom. Black type stamped onto it hard enough to read across a counter. A buffalo pressed into the paper rather than printed over it. And a five-stop heat scale printed along the edge, top and bottom, bracketing everything in between. Once that image is in mind, every rule in this document follows from it: why the ground is loud, why the chrome is parchment instead of white, why the mark darkens rather than lightens, and why nothing floats.

Hot, printed, engineered. The ground is genuinely saturated, and that is the brand: the live site samples at 237 instances of the orange against 183 of black, so a timid neutral page would be a different restaurant. What keeps a saturated page from reading as a flyer is that every loud move is governed by a stated rule with a measured number behind it. The orange is unusable as type on this ground at 1.8:1, so it is never type on this ground. The focus ring is ink on light and orange on dark because the ring's neighbours are the ground on both sides once it is offset. The destructive red is two steps down its own hue because signage red cannot carry a label.

Nothing in this system is decorative by accident. The grain exists because a gradient this smooth bands on an 8-bit panel. The buffalo is a single bold silhouette because a detailed engraving collapses into a smudge at watermark opacity. The one authored animation on the site is the heat scale drawing itself, which is the product's own mechanism moving, not a fade applied to seven sections in turn.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed warm gradient ground, with dark surfaces sitting on it. That contrast is the layout.
Anton in caps for every heading, Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono for every number.
No shadows except one warm offset under the sticky chrome.
A five-stop heat ramp that is the same five swatches everywhere it appears.
Every colour pair carries a measured contrast ratio, and the ratio decided the value.

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only loud colour. Yellow and red are accents with narrow, stated jobs. Nothing else in this system gets a colour at all.

rules.name: The Orange Is For Dark Rule
rules.body: Buffalo Orange on the amber ground measures 1.8:1 and on parchment 2.6:1. It is therefore never type on a light surface. It may appear on a light surface only as a graphic: a rule, an underline, a fill. On ink it measures 5.4:1 and is for headings, prices, buttons and icons, never for paragraphs.

rules.name: The Ground Owns the Ring Rule
rules.body: The focus ring colour belongs to the surface, not to the control. Ink is the default, at 7.6:1 on the darkest stop of the gradient, and dark surfaces flip it to orange, at 6.0:1 on ink. This is keyed off the background utility at zero specificity, so a charcoal card added next year gets a legible ring without anyone remembering to ask for one.

rules.name: The Never Adjacent Rule
rules.body: Orange text never sits on red, and red never sits on orange.

rules.name: The Tracking Scales With the Type Rule
rules.body: The display class carries +0.005em, which is what a condensed face needs at label size. Left unchanged at 96px that same value opens the word up, so each tier takes back more of it as it grows, down to a floor of -0.015em. Never set tracking once and apply it across sizes.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: If a value is a price, a code, a countdown, a quantity or a percentage, it is JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. No exceptions, because these appear beside each other in columns and in receipts.

rules.name: The Bloom Correction Rule
rules.body: Light type on a near-black ground blooms: counters close and letterforms spread. Dark surfaces therefore add 0.006em of tracking to untracked reading copy, applied at the surface at zero specificity so a new dark card inherits it and anything stating its own tracking keeps it.

rules.name: The Sixteen Pixel Rule
rules.body: Form controls are 16px below the sm breakpoint. Anything smaller makes iOS Safari zoom the viewport on focus, which on a checkout form reads as the page jumping.

rules.name: The Value, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by lightness. Do not add a shadow or a border to something that is already 11:1 away from what is behind it.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a shadow is genuinely needed, it is brown and offset. A neutral grey shadow on a warm page reads as dirt.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: New components take 0.4rem unless there is a stated geometric reason not to. A system with five radii in play reads as five systems.

rules.name: The Real Edge Or Nothing Rule
rules.body: The amber ground is so light and so saturated that nothing subtle survives on it. Ink at 40% measures 2.3:1 against the gradient, so there is no soft plate available here. A control either takes a real edge or it takes none.

rules.name: The States Differ Structurally Rule
rules.body: Before adding a colour to distinguish a state, check whether the state already differs in structure. A ready order carries an orange heading, orange bars and a six-line orange code; a stopped one has no code and no ladder at all. A coloured stripe on top of that says something the screen has already said twice, and one card wearing a stripe that no other card wears reads as a component from a different product.

rules.name: The Press Is Shared Rule
rules.body: Anything a finger can press answers with the same 2% scale on the same timing, whether it is a button, a chip, a flavour tile or a pickup window. Selection controls are not buttons, but they are pressable, and the feel has to agree.

rules.name: The Full Thing Stays On Screen Rule
rules.body: A sold-out flavour, a taken pickup window and an out-of-stock item go flat, not away. Removing them makes the interface look broken and hides the information that the shop is busy.

rules.name: The Header Is In The Fold Rule
rules.body: The header is sticky top-0 and therefore still in flow, so the first screen is the hero plus the bar above it. A hero sized to fill the viewport actually overfills it. Size it to leave roughly an eighth of the viewport to the next section, so the page reads as having more below rather than ending at a seam.

rules.name: The One Heat Surface Per Page Rule
rules.body: A level is the same swatch everywhere, and that is the point of the fixed ramp. The ramp itself is drawn once per page, in the place where somebody is choosing a level. This replaces an earlier rule that permitted two surfaces provided they differed in shape: changing the shape of a restatement does not stop it being one, and the second surface is always the one further from the decision, which is the one to cut.

rules.name: The Moment Belongs To The Band Rule
rules.body: The five bars extending in sequence is the site's only authored animation and it lives where somebody is choosing. Nothing else on the landing page draws the ramp at all, so the band's entrance is the first time a visitor sees the object move, which is what the rule was protecting all along.

rules.name: The Ink Layer Takes the Surface's Colour Rule
rules.body: A mural asset never carries a colour of its own. It is traced to currentColor and rendered through a CSS mask, so one file serves char on amber, bone on charcoal and orange as a graphic. A flattened black-on-white export is wrong twice over: on the amber ground it paints the white rectangle this system does not have, and on a charcoal card it draws black on black. An SVG loaded through cannot do this either, because that document is isolated and currentColor resolves against nothing there.

rules.name: The One Drawn Scene Per Page Rule
rules.body: The One Heat Surface Per Page Rule, generalised. A heat level keeps its swatch everywhere and a drawing keeps its lines everywhere, but the same form appears once per page. Two street scenes on one route is not a statement and its restatement, it is a repeat. The footer's skyline does not count as the second: it is a filled silhouette off the packaging doing a mark's job, chrome that brackets every page the way the heat rule does. Count scenes, not drawings.

rules.name: The Landscape Crop Needs A Landscape Hole Rule
rules.body: A mural asset is a wide crop of a wall, and cover scales it by whichever dimension of its box demands more. On a portrait viewport that is always the height and it is not close: the landing hero's right-hand placement is 1600 by 1187 of artwork, and a 768x1024 tablet hands it a 399 by 800 hole, which renders the drawing 1078 wide and throws 679 of that away. So a placement like this is gated on min-aspect-ratio, not on a width breakpoint, which cannot tell a portrait tablet from a laptop. Below the gate there is no drawing at all, and that is correct rather than degraded: on a portrait viewport the copy is the full width of the section, so there is no region beside it for a wall to occupy.

rules.name: The Hatching Stays Strokes Rule
rules.body: Facade hatching is discrete strokes and never a tone. It is about ten pixels wide against an eighteen thousand pixel source, so scaling a whole scene to a phone puts it under one device pixel and a sub-pixel ink line is a wash. There is no neutral grey in this system and no honest way to arrive at one. The fix is upstream every time: crop to a smaller subject, or export a variant with the fine strokes removed at the bitmap by a morphological opening. The full street canyon cannot be shown below roughly 1830px with its hatching intact, which is why no placement shows the full canyon.

rules.name: The Drawing Runs Off The Page Rule
rules.body: A mural asset is a crop of a wall, so its own boundary is a straight line that means nothing. Sized to sit inside a column it reads as a framed picture laid on the page. Every large placement bleeds off the edges of whatever clips it, using cover rather than contain, because contain fits the whole drawing in the box and leaves bare ground around the remainder. Any edge left inside the page is faded to nothing rather than cut, by intersecting a gradient into the mask; that lowers the strokes' alpha without merging them into a tone. Two corollaries: write mask-* and -webkit-mask-* from one source, because the aliases are one property and a spread override silently keeps the prefixed default; and a skyline that must span a width it was not drawn for needs a second drawing, not a stretch and not a repeat.

rules.name: The Drawing Darkens the Ground Rule
rules.body: Where the artwork sits behind content it darkens, as ink at low alpha, the way the buffalo does at 9%. That is what makes it read as printed into the page rather than pasted onto it. Where the artwork is the content it takes the surface's reading colour and may lighten, as it does in bone on a charcoal card. The test is whether anything must stay legible on top of it: behind type it darkens, and the alpha is whatever keeps that type above 4.5:1. On the no-photo tile that alpha is 14%, measuring 4.68:1 against char in the worst case, a solid marker stroke directly behind a letter.

rules.name: The Fourth Face Letters, It Does Not Set Rule
rules.body: This system used to ban a fourth typeface outright, which was right about the risk and wrong about the shape. A brand script has one legitimate job here and it is a logo's job: lettering a fixed phrase the store already draws that way. The face is admitted for exactly that. If a string is variable, or is a heading, a label, a control or a number, it is Anton, Inter or JetBrains Mono, because the type scale was measured against Anton's metrics and none of that transfers. Three faces set the interface; the fourth only letters.

dos: Do put dark surfaces on the amber ground. That contrast is the layout, and alternating bare ground with full-bleed dark bands is how a page gets its structure here.
Do measure every new colour pair and record the ratio. Every value in this system has one behind it.

Do composite a colour through a 1x1 canvas and read the pixel back when checking contrast programmatically. Tailwind v4 emits oklch() and naive RGB parsing of getComputedStyle produces fake failures near 1.1:1.
Do use 2.75rem as the minimum interactive height, everywhere.
Do let the ground set the focus ring, and let the tone prop set it on a control that knows better than its surroundings.
Do set text colour on a dark container and let its contents inherit, rather than declaring a colour on every leaf.
Do use transform-only hover and press effects, so nothing reflows.
Do use the heat ramp's five fixed swatches wherever a heat level appears.
Do spend motion on the product's own mechanisms rather than on arrivals, and make the drawn or finished state the default so no-JS and reduced motion both keep it.
Do let states differ structurally before reaching for a colour to distinguish them.
Do key short-viewport rules on max-height, never on width. A landscape phone at 844x390 is past every width breakpoint while having under 300px of usable height.
Do let a mural asset inherit its colour from the surface, through a CSS mask over background-color: currentColor.
Do export a separate simplified variant when a hatched motif has to render small, rather than scaling the detailed one.
Do measure the alpha of any drawing that sits behind type, and keep the type above 4.5:1.
donts: Don't set Buffalo Orange as type on any light surface. It measures 1.8:1 on the amber ground and 2.6:1 on parchment. As a graphic it is fine.
Don't use signage red for anything but the top of the heat scale and a hover accent. A destructive fill takes Red Deep.
Don't put orange text on red or red text on orange.
Don't add a border or a shadow to a surface already separated by value.
Don't use a neutral grey anywhere. Not in a shadow, not in a hairline, not in a disabled state.
Don't implement a focus ring as a box-shadow. Any component that sets its own shadow silently defeats it. Focus is an outline, 3px, offset 2px.
Don't set a form control below 16px on a phone.
Don't set the display face below 0.75rem, or above 6rem.

Don't apply a blanket entrance animation to sections as they scroll. Motion is earned by meaning here, and a fade applied to seven sections in turn says nothing about any of them. Motion that animates the product's own mechanism, the way the heat scale draws its five stops, is exactly what this system wants more of.
Don't introduce a second radius scale or a second accent colour.
Don't widen the fourth typeface past the tagline. It is admitted to letter one fixed phrase and it sets nothing.

Don't ship a mural asset with a colour baked into it, and don't reach for to load one. Both produce the same failure: a drawing that cannot take its surface's colour, which is a white box on the amber ground and an invisible one on a charcoal card.
Don't make a hatched drawing smaller by scaling it. Below about a pixel the strokes stop being strokes. Crop to a smaller subject or export a culled variant.
Don't put a drawn scene on the order tracker or the confirmation screen. The States Differ Structurally Rule already covers it.
Don't paper the site in mural. One drawn scene per page, on pages that have room for one, and the amber gradient keeps doing the structural work.
Don't size a mural asset to fit inside its column. It is a crop of a wall, so a visible boundary reads as a framed picture. Bleed it off the edges and fade any edge that still falls inside the page.
